rationale: The answer covers both key points. Key point 1 (board inquiries into causes and corrective options, spreads against peers, AP/market-maker participation): it calls for peer comparison with similar holdings, benchmarks and trading hours, and for assessing spreads, depth and volatility. It also says to interview APs and market makers about quoting, inventory, hedging, creation/redemption activity and participation concentration, and it lists corrective options (disclosures, better valuation/trading data, liquidity-provider outreach, operational changes). Key point 2 (frictions that explain deviations without arbitrage failure): it addresses stale NAV inputs, fair-value adjustments, time zones and market-hour differences, holdings that stop trading before the ETF, closing-auction effects, underlying tradability and trading costs, creation/redemption costs, and settlement constraints. It proposes an inquiry rather than a single presumed cause and explicitly rejects relying on a single numerical trigger, consistent with the grader note that the 2% figure is not a general trigger. No material errors found. Mentioning time zones for a US equity ETF is slightly incidental but not wrong.
